title: Machine learning prioritizes blood markers associated with neuralgia and depressive symptoms
summary: LASSO and random forest prioritized four blood-expression markers shared by postherpetic-neuralgia and depression datasets. A separate 240-person clinical study found higher candidate-marker expression in neuralgia with depressive symptoms; serum LTF/sCD40L discrimination had AUC 0.818 within the 120 neuralgia patients. Symptoms were defined by PHQ-9 rather than a formal psychiatric interview. These are candidate associations, not a causal pain–depression mechanism or validated clinical diagnosis. The public-data four-gene model was refitted in its comparison cohort, so it was not fixed-coefficient external validation.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection; random forest; logistic biomarker modeling
organization: Shanxi Medical University; The People’s Hospital of Chongzuo; Sun Yat-sen University; Foshan Women and Children Hospital; Southern Medical University; South China University of Technology

evidence.tested: Learned selection of LTF, HLA-DPA1, CACNA2D4 and CD40LG was followed by new human blood expression/protein assays in four clinical groups of 60 each. Within PHN-only participants (n=120), the combined serum marker score had AUC 0.818 for PHQ-9-defined symptoms.
evidence.unknown: Cross-sectional biomarkers and symptom thresholds do not prove causality, formal MDD diagnosis, prospective screening benefit or treatment effects. The discovery transcriptomic cohorts are small and initial screening exploratory. Public-data comparison coefficients were re-estimated.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO and random forest prioritize the transcriptomic candidates subsequently measured as human clinical biomarkers. Learned selection is distinct from WGCNA/network enrichment and from the later descriptive clinical associations.

source_review.scope: Primary source-provenanced article text independently read for transcriptomic model selection, coefficient-refit limitation, human clinical cohort/assays/results, limitations, affiliations and date. The represented claim concerns human biomarker associations; no animal intervention efficacy is claimed. No underlying-data reanalysis.
